text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The struggle to establish the motive for killing Malawi army general Manken Chigawa by his family seems to be hitting a blank wall as police seem to be holding information at the on-going inquest in Zomba, southern Malawi. General Chigawa was gunned down by alleged petty car thieves early last year.

- More than 200 Asylum seekers from various African countries at Dzaleka refugee camp in Dowa, central Malawi, have defied rules and picked up jobs in Malawi. An official in the Relief and Rehabilitation ministry, Humphrey Nthara, said the population for refugees at Dzalenka has dropped to 942 from 1,200 after some ventured into running businesses or secured local jobs outside the camp contrary to entry regulations. Refugees are not allowed free movement in their host country.
